narrative:
The model predicted that you have a 68.9% chance of failing the bar exam on your first attempt. Because this probability is well above the acceptance threshold, your law school application was rejected.

The decision was driven primarily by three factors from your academic record. Your class ranking at the end of your third year was the strongest influence and pushed the prediction strongly toward failure. Standing in the bottom decile is far below the average of accepted students (around the middle of the class), signaling that your performance in the later, more demanding years of college was unusually weak. Your first-year ranking in the bottom decile had a similar but smaller negative effect.

Your LSAT score of 37 worked in the opposite direction. It is almost exactly at the average of students who were admitted, so it helped pull the prediction back toward passing. Unfortunately, this positive signal was not large enough to overcome the impact of your low class rankings.

Given these results, you should focus on strengthening the areas the model weighed most heavily. Retaking courses to improve your GPA, seeking structured bar-prep support, or considering schools with different admissions criteria could improve your chances in a future application.
